tip.tr: I için am, he/she/it için is, you/we/they için are kullanılır. Olumsuz için not ekleriz: She is not tired.

items.text: I am a student.
She is very tired.
I ___ from Turkey.
We are not at home.
They ___ my neighbours.
Are you ready?
___ he a doctor?
The cat is in the garden.
My brothers ___ not at school.
He is not my friend.
It ___ not cold today.
Is your mother at home?

explain.tr:
“Be” fiili, kim olduğunu, nasıl olduğunu veya nerede olduğunu söylemek için kullanılır.
Kalıp: I am, he/she/it is, you/we/they are.
Olumsuz için not ekleriz: She is not (isn't) at home.
Soru için fiili öne alırız: Are you ready?
Sık yapılan hata: Türkçede “be” gerekmez (“Ben öğrenciyim”), ama İngilizcede unutulmaz: I am a student, “I student” değil.
explain.en:
The verb “be” tells who or what someone is, how they feel, or where they are.
Pattern: I am, he/she/it is, you/we/they are.
For negatives add not: She is not (isn't) at home.
For questions, put the verb first: Are you ready?
Common mistake: Turkish has no separate word for “be”, so learners say “I student”. Always say: I am a student.

tip.tr: I, he, she, it için was; you, we, they için were kullanılır. Örnek: I was at home. They were happy.

items.text: I was at home yesterday.
They were on holiday last week.
My parents ___ at work this morning.

native.tr: Annem ve babam bu sabah işteydi.

items.text: The weather was cold yesterday.
I ___ not at the party.
We were not tired.
___ they happy with the food?
Were you at school yesterday?
It ___ a great day.
She was not ill yesterday.
The shops ___ closed on Sunday.
Was the film good?

explain.tr:
Geçmişte kim olduğunu, nasıl olduğunu veya nerede olduğunu anlatmak için was/were kullanırız.
Kalıp: I/he/she/it was; you/we/they were.
Olumsuz: was not (wasn't), were not (weren't). Soru: Were you tired?
Sık yapılan hata: “I were” demek. Doğrusu: I was. “You was” da yanlıştır: You were.
explain.en:
We use was/were to say who, how or where someone or something was in the past.
Pattern: I/he/she/it was; you/we/they were.
Negative: was not (wasn't), were not (weren't). Question: Were you tired?
Common mistake: saying “I were”. The correct form is I was, and “you was” is wrong too: you were.

examples.text: We were in Izmir last week.

native.en: We were in Izmir last week.

tip.tr: Şu anda olan şeyler için am/is/are + fiil-ing kullanılır. Örnek: She is reading a book.

items.text: I am drinking water.
She is watching television now.
I ___ going to school now.
The children are playing in the garden.
He ___ sleeping at the moment.
We are not cooking dinner.
They are ___ football.
What are you reading?
She is not ___ a book.
My mother is working in the kitchen.
Are you ___ to music?
Is it raining?

explain.tr:
Şu anda olan veya bu günlerde süren işler için kullanılır.
Kalıp: am/is/are + fiil-ing (I am working).
Olumsuz: She is not working. Soru: Are you working?
Sık yapılan hata: am/is/are'i unutmak. “I working” değil, I am working denir.
explain.en:
We use it for things happening right now or around now.
Pattern: am/is/are + verb-ing (I am working).
Negative: She is not working. Question: Are you working?
Common mistake: forgetting am/is/are. Say I am working, not “I working”.

title.tr: Geniş zaman: I go, she goes

tip.tr: Alışkanlıklar için geniş zaman kullanılır; he/she/it ile fiile -s eklenir. Olumsuz ve soru için do/does kullanılır: She does not go. Do you go?

items.text: I drink tea every day.
She goes to school by bus.
My sister ___ in a bank.
We do not eat meat.
They ___ like fish.
My father does not like coffee.
___ she play tennis?
Do you speak English?
He does not ___ milk.
Does Ali live in London?
We ___ breakfast at eight.
My cat drinks milk.

explain.tr:
Alışkanlıklar, günlük işler ve genel doğrular için kullanılır.
Kalıp: fiilin yalın hali; he/she/it ile -s eklenir (she works).
Olumsuz ve soru: do/does kullanırız (I do not work. Does she work?). Does varken fiile -s gelmez.
Sık yapılan hata: “She work” demek ya da “Does she works?” demek.
explain.en:
We use it for habits, daily routines and general facts.
Pattern: the base verb; add -s for he/she/it (she works).
Negatives and questions use do/does (I do not work. Does she work?). After does, the verb has no -s.
Common mistake: saying “She work” or “Does she works?”.

tip.tr: Bir şeyin var olduğunu söylemek için tekilde there is, çoğulda there are kullanılır. Örnek: There is a book. There are two books.

items.text: There is a table in the room.
There are two children in the park.
There ___ a cat on the sofa.
There is not a book in my bag.
There ___ three bedrooms in our house.
Is there a museum in the city?
___ there a bank near here?

native.tr: Buraya yakın bir banka var mı?

items.text: There are not any apples on the table.
There are not ___ chairs in the room.
How many students are there?
There ___ not any water in the bottle.
There is some milk at home.

explain.tr:
Bir yerde bir şeyin var olduğunu söylemek için kullanılır.
Tekil ve sayılamayan: there is (There is a cat). Çoğul: there are (There are two cats).
Olumsuz: There is not / There are not. Soru: Is there a bank near here?
Sık yapılan hata: “It has a park” demek. “Burada bir park var” için There is a park here denir.
explain.en:
We use it to say that something exists somewhere.
Singular and uncountable: there is (There is a cat). Plural: there are (There are two cats).
Negative: There is not / There are not. Question: Is there a bank near here?
Common mistake: saying “It has a park”. To say a park exists, use There is a park here.

examples.text: There is a shop on my street.

native.en: There is a shop on my street.

examples.text: There are three eggs in the fridge.

native.en: There are three eggs in the fridge.

tip.tr: What (ne), where (nerede), who (kim), when (ne zaman), why (neden), how (nasıl) soru başında gelir. Örnek: Where do you live?

items.text: What is your name?
Where is the school?
___ is your teacher?
Who is that man?
___ is your birthday? It is in May.
When is your birthday?
___ are you from? I am from Izmir.
Why are you sad?
___ do you like this song? Because it is nice.

native.tr: Bu şarkıyı neden seviyorsun? Çünkü güzel.

items.text: How are you today?
___ old are you?
Where do you live?

explain.tr:
Soru kelimeleri bilgi istemek için cümlenin başına gelir: what (ne), where (nerede), who (kim), when (ne zaman), why (neden), how (nasıl).
Kalıp: soru kelimesi + do/does/am/is/are + özne + fiil (Where do you live?).
Sık yapılan hata: Türkçedeki gibi soru kelimesini sona koymak. “You live where?” değil, Where do you live? denir.
explain.en:
Question words start a sentence when you ask for information: what, where, who, when, why, how.
Pattern: question word + do/does/am/is/are + subject + verb (Where do you live?).
Common mistake: putting the question word at the end like in Turkish. Say Where do you live?, not “You live where?”.

tip.tr: Yapabilmek için can + fiil kullanılır; fiile -s eklenmez. Olumsuzu cannot. Örnek: She can swim. I cannot swim.

items.text: I can swim.
She can play the guitar.
My brother ___ run very fast.
We cannot come today.
I cannot ___ the answer.
Can you drive a car?
___ you help me, please?
Birds can fly.
She can ___ three languages.
My father cannot speak English.
Fish ___ walk.
Can I park here?

explain.tr:
“Can” bir şeyi yapabildiğini veya izin olduğunu söyler.
Kalıp: özne + can + fiilin yalın hali (He can swim). Olumsuz: cannot (can't). Soru: Can you help me?
Sık yapılan hata: Fiile -s, to ya da -ing eklemek. “She can to swim” veya “She cans swim” yanlıştır: She can swim.
explain.en:
“Can” says what you are able to do, or that something is allowed.
Pattern: subject + can + base verb (He can swim). Negative: cannot (can't). Question: Can you help me?
Common mistake: adding -s, to or -ing. “She can to swim” and “She cans swim” are wrong: She can swim.

examples.text: I can speak a little English.

native.en: I can speak a little English.

tip.tr: I, you, we, they ile have; he, she, it ile has kullanılır. Olumsuz ve soru için do/does gerekir: She does not have a car. Do you have a pen?

items.text: I have a dog.
She has two sisters.
My mother ___ a new phone.
We do not have a car.
I ___ two brothers.
Ali does not have a computer.
Do you ___ any money?
Do you have a pen?
She does not ___ a car.
Does he have a bike?
___ they have a garden?
They have a big house.

explain.tr:
“Have” sahip olmayı anlatır: bir şeyin, bir ailenin ya da bir hastalığın olması.
I/you/we/they ile have, he/she/it ile has kullanılır.
Olumsuz ve soru için do/does gerekir: I do not have a car. Does she have a pen?
Sık yapılan hata: “She have” demek. Doğrusu: She has. Does varken de has değil have gelir.
explain.en:
“Have” shows possession: owning something, having family, or having an illness.
Use have with I/you/we/they and has with he/she/it.
Negatives and questions need do/does: I do not have a car. Does she have a pen?
Common mistake: saying “She have”. Say She has. After does, use have, not has.

tip.tr: Geçmiş olayları anlatırken düzenli fiillere -ed eklenir (cook → cooked), düzensizlerin ise özel biçimi vardır (go → went). Soru ve olumsuzda did / did not + fiilin yalın hali kullanılır: I did not go.

items.text: We ate pizza last night.
I did not go to the shop yesterday.
She ___ a letter to her friend yesterday.
Ali bought a new phone last week.

native.tr: Ali geçen hafta yeni bir telefon aldı.

items.text: ___ you like the film?
Did you watch a film last night?

native.tr: Dün gece bir film izledin mi?

items.text: My mother cooked dinner this evening.
We ___ tired after the long walk.
They did not come to our house yesterday.
He did not ___ the bus.
I woke up early this morning.
They ___ to the beach last summer.

explain.tr:
Geçmişte bitmiş olayları anlatmak için kullanılır (yesterday, last week, in 2020).
Düzenli fiillere -ed eklenir (walk → walked); düzensizlerin özel biçimi vardır (go → went).
Olumsuz ve soruda did + yalın fiil kullanılır: I did not go. Did you go?
Sık yapılan hata: did varken fiili de geçmişe çevirmek. “Did you went?” değil, Did you go?
explain.en:
We use it for finished events in the past (yesterday, last week, in 2020).
Regular verbs take -ed (walk → walked); irregular verbs change form (go → went).
Negatives and questions use did + base verb: I did not go. Did you go?
Common mistake: putting the past form after did. Say Did you go?, not “Did you went?”.

examples.text: I watched a film last night.

native.en: I watched a film last night.

examples.text: She went to Ankara by bus.

native.en: She went to Ankara by bus.

tip.tr: Plan ve tahminler için am / is / are + going to + fiil kullanılır: I am going to study tonight. Olumsuzda not eklenir: She is not going to come.

items.text: I am going to visit my friend tomorrow.
It is going to rain.
Look at those clouds! It ___ going to rain.
What are you going to do this weekend?
I ___ going to learn English this year.
We are not going to cook tonight.
Ahmet is going to be a doctor.
They are going to ___ a party on Saturday.
Are you going to buy a new car?
She ___ not going to come to the meeting.
I am going to sleep early tonight.
Are you ___ to wait for me?

explain.tr:
Önceden planladığın şeyleri ve belirtilere dayanan tahminleri anlatır.
Kalıp: am/is/are + going to + fiilin yalın hali (I am going to study).
Olumsuz: She is not going to come. Soru: Are you going to eat?
Sık yapılan hata: am/is/are'i unutmak ya da to'dan sonra -ing eklemek. “I going to eat” değil, I am going to eat.
explain.en:
It talks about plans you already made, and predictions based on what you can see.
Pattern: am/is/are + going to + base verb (I am going to study).
Negative: She is not going to come. Question: Are you going to eat?
Common mistake: forgetting am/is/are. Say I am going to eat, not “I going to eat”.

examples.text: I am going to call my mother tonight.

native.en: I am going to call my mother tonight.

examples.text: They are going to move next month.

native.en: They are going to move next month.

examples.text: Look at the sky. It is going to rain.

native.en: Look at the sky. It is going to rain.

examples.text: Are you going to buy that bag?

native.en: Are you going to buy that bag?

tip.tr: Anlık kararlar, söz ve tahminler için will + fiil kullanılır: I will help you. Olumsuzu will not (kısaca won't) şeklindedir; fiil her zaman yalın haldedir.

items.text: I will call you tomorrow.
We will help you with your homework.
I ___ open the window because it is hot in here.
It will be sunny tomorrow.
It is cold. I think it ___ snow tonight.

native.tr: Hava soğuk. Bence bu gece kar yağacak.

items.text: I will not answer this question.
I think you will pass the exam.
She will ___ you the answer later.
Will you come to school tomorrow?
We ___ not forget your birthday.
He will not be late.
___ you help me carry this bag?

native.tr: Bu çantayı taşımama yardım eder misin?

explain.tr:
“Will” anlık kararlar, sözler ve gelecek tahminleri için kullanılır.
Kalıp: özne + will + yalın fiil (I will help you). Olumsuz: will not (won't). Soru: Will you come?
Tüm özneler için aynıdır, -s almaz.
Sık yapılan hata: “He wills go” ya da “will to go” demek. Doğrusu: He will go.
explain.en:
“Will” is for quick decisions, promises and predictions about the future.
Pattern: subject + will + base verb (I will help you). Negative: will not (won't). Question: Will you come?
It is the same for all subjects and never takes -s.
Common mistake: saying “He wills go” or “will to go”. Say He will go.

examples.text: I will carry that bag for you.

native.en: I will carry that bag for you.

tip.tr: Kısa sıfatlara -er / -est eklenir (tall → taller → the tallest), uzun sıfatlarda more / the most kullanılır (more interesting). Karşılaştırmada than gelir: bigger than.

items.text: This bag is heavier than that one.
He is the tallest boy in the class.
My brother is ___ than me.
Ankara is smaller than Istanbul.
This is the ___ day of the year.
This film is more interesting than the other one.
She is my best friend.
English is ___ than maths for me.

native.tr: Bana göre İngilizce matematikten daha kolay.

items.text: It is hotter today than yesterday.
Today is ___ than yesterday.
This is the most expensive watch in the world.
She is the ___ person I know.

explain.tr:
İki şeyi karşılaştırmak için sıfatın karşılaştırma biçimi, en üstünü söylemek için en üstünlük biçimi kullanılır.
Kısa sıfatlar: -er / the -est (tall → taller → the tallest). Uzun sıfatlar: more / the most (more interesting). Karşılaştırmada than gelir.
Sık yapılan hata: “more taller” gibi ikisini birlikte kullanmak. Doğrusu: taller.
explain.en:
We use comparative forms to compare two things and superlative forms to say which is the most.
Short adjectives: -er / the -est (tall → taller → the tallest). Long adjectives: more / the most (more interesting). Use than when comparing.
Common mistake: mixing both, like “more taller”. Say taller.

examples.text: My bag is heavier than yours.

native.en: My bag is heavier than yours.

examples.text: This book is more interesting than that one.

native.en: This book is more interesting than that one.

examples.text: He is the tallest boy in the class.

native.en: He is the tallest boy in the class.

examples.text: Today is the hottest day of the year.

native.en: Today is the hottest day of the year.

tip.tr: Zorunluluk için must veya have to, tavsiye için should kullanılır: You should rest. Must not yasak, do not have to ise zorunlu olmama demektir. Geçmişte had to kullanılır.

items.text: I have to get up early tomorrow.
You should drink more water.
You ___ stop at a red light.
You must not smoke here.
She ___ to work on Sundays.
I had to work last night.
We do not have to go to school tomorrow.
You look tired. You ___ rest.
You should see a doctor.
I ___ not have to pay for the bus.

native.tr: Otobüs için ödeme yapmak zorunda değilim.

items.text: Ali has to wear a uniform.
Students ___ not use phones in the exam.

explain.tr:
Must ve have to zorunluluğu, should ise tavsiyeyi anlatır.
Kalıp: must/should + yalın fiil (You should rest). Have to fiil gibi çekilir: She has to work.
Dikkat: must not yasak demektir, do not have to ise “zorunda değilsin” demektir. Geçmişte had to kullanılır.
Sık yapılan hata: “must to go” demek. Doğrusu: must go.
explain.en:
Must and have to show necessity; should gives advice.
Pattern: must/should + base verb (You should rest). Have to changes like a normal verb: She has to work.
Note: must not means it is forbidden, but do not have to means it is not necessary. In the past, use had to.
Common mistake: saying “must to go”. Say must go.

examples.text: I have to wake up early tomorrow.

native.en: I have to wake up early tomorrow.

tip.tr: Saat ve belirli noktalar için at (at nine), günler için on (on Monday), ay, yıl ve mevsimler için in (in May). Yer için: at bir nokta (at school), in bir alan veya şehir (in Istanbul), on bir yüzey (on the table).

items.text: The lesson starts at nine.
My birthday is in May.
We have lunch ___ noon.
I will see the doctor on Monday.
She was born ___ 1998.
My keys are on the table.
My brother is at school now.
The film starts ___ Friday evening.
We live in Istanbul.
There is a picture ___ the wall.
I usually go to bed late at night.
I met him ___ the bus stop.

explain.tr:
In, on ve at zaman ve yer bildirir.
Zaman: at saat için (at nine), on gün için (on Monday), in ay, yıl ve mevsim için (in May).
Yer: at bir nokta (at school), on bir yüzey (on the table), in bir alan veya şehir (in Istanbul).
Sık yapılan hata: Türkçedeki -de/-da eki tek olduğu için hepsini aynı sanmak. “In Monday” değil, on Monday denir.
explain.en:
In, on and at show time and place.
Time: at for clock times (at nine), on for days (on Monday), in for months, years and seasons (in May).
Place: at for a point (at school), on for a surface (on the table), in for an area or city (in Istanbul).
Common mistake: Turkish uses one ending (-de/-da) for all of these, so learners mix them up. Say on Monday, not “in Monday”.

examples.text: The meeting is at three o'clock.

native.en: The meeting is at three o'clock.

examples.text: The keys are on the table.

native.en: The keys are on the table.

tip.tr: Olumlu cümlede some, olumsuz ve soruda any kullanılır. Sayılabilenlerle many (many books), sayılamayanlarla much (much water) gelir.

items.text: I have some water in my bag.
There is not any bread at home.
Do you have ___ brothers or sisters?
How many brothers do you have?
There is too ___ traffic in the morning.
How much milk do you want?
I have a lot of work today.
We need ___ eggs for the cake.

native.tr: Pasta için biraz yumurtaya ihtiyacımız var.

items.text: Would you like some tea?
How ___ people came to the party?
There are not many parks in the city.
I do not have ___ money today.

explain.tr:
Some, any, much ve many miktar bildirir.
Olumlu cümlede some, olumsuz ve soruda any kullanılır. Sayılabilenlerle many (many books), sayılamayanlarla much (much water) gelir.
Sık yapılan hata: “many water” demek. Su sayılamaz, bu yüzden much water denir.
explain.en:
Some, any, much and many talk about quantity.
Use some in positive sentences and any in negatives and questions. Use many with countable nouns (many books) and much with uncountable nouns (much water).
Common mistake: saying “many water”. Water is uncountable, so say much water.

examples.text: I have some friends in London.

native.en: I have some friends in London.

examples.text: How many students are in your class?

native.en: How many students are in your class?

tip.tr: have/has + üçüncü fiil (V3) ile geçmişte başlayan ya da şimdiyle bağlantılı olayları anlatırız. Örnek: I have already eaten (Çoktan yedim).

items.text: I have never been to Paris.
She has already finished her work.
My sister ___ never eaten sushi.
We have not eaten yet.
I ___ lived in this city since 2015.
I have just received a message.
Have you finished your homework ___?
Have you ever been to England?
They have ___ gone to the airport.
Tom has lived here for three years.
We have ___ that film twice.
My brother has not opened the door.

explain.tr:
Geçmişte olup şimdiyle bağlantılı olayları, yaşam deneyimlerini ve “henüz/çoktan” durumlarını anlatır.
Kalıp: have/has + üçüncü fiil (V3) (I have finished). Olumsuz: has not. Soru: Have you ever been to Rome?
Zamanı belli geçmiş olaylarda (yesterday) kullanılmaz.
Sık yapılan hata: “I have seen him yesterday” demek. Doğrusu: I saw him yesterday.
explain.en:
It describes past events connected to now, life experiences, and things “already” or “not yet” done.
Pattern: have/has + past participle (V3) (I have finished). Negative: has not. Question: Have you ever been to Rome?
Do not use it with a finished time like yesterday.
Common mistake: “I have seen him yesterday”. Say I saw him yesterday.

examples.text: We have never been to Spain.

native.en: We have never been to Spain.

examples.text: Have you finished your homework yet?

native.en: Have you finished your homework yet?

tip.tr: was/were + fiil-ing, geçmişte belli bir anda devam eden eylemi anlatır. when kısa olayı, while uzun süren eylemi bağlar. Örnek: I was reading when you called.

alt: While I was showering the phone rang.
items.text: The phone rang while I was showering.
They were playing football last night.
I ___ TV when the lights went out.

alt: When I called were you sleeping?
items.text: Were you sleeping when I called?
What ___ you doing at nine last night?
My mother was cooking dinner.
He broke his arm while he ___ football.

alt: While it was raining we were walking.
items.text: We were walking while it was raining.
The children ___ in the garden when it started to rain.
She was not looking at me.
It ___ snowing when we left home.

alt: While we were working the teacher came in.
items.text: The teacher came in while we were working.

explain.tr:
Geçmişte belli bir anda devam etmekte olan eylemi anlatır.
Kalıp: was/were + fiil-ing (I was reading). Olumsuz: was not. Soru: Were you sleeping?
Kısa bir olay araya girerse when, uzun iki eylem birlikte sürerse while kullanılır.
Sık yapılan hata: “I was read” demek. Fiile -ing eklemeyi unutma: I was reading.
explain.en:
It describes an action that was in progress at a certain moment in the past.
Pattern: was/were + verb-ing (I was reading). Negative: was not. Question: Were you sleeping?
Use when with a short interrupting event, and while for a longer action.
Common mistake: saying “I was read”. Add -ing: I was reading.

examples.text: I was cooking when you called.

native.en: I was cooking when you called.

examples.text: It was raining while we were walking.

native.en: It was raining while we were walking.

examples.text: What were you doing at eight?

native.en: What were you doing at eight?

tip.tr: Gerçek ihtimal: if + şimdiki zaman, will + fiil. Hayali durum: if + geçmiş zaman, would + fiil. Örnek: If it rains, I will stay home.

alt: If it rains I will stay home.
items.text: I will stay home if it rains.

alt: If I had money I would travel.

explain.tr:
If cümleleri bir şartı ve sonucunu anlatır.
Gerçek ihtimal: if + şimdiki zaman, will + fiil (If it rains, I will stay home). Hayali durum: if + geçmiş zaman, would + fiil (If I had money, I would travel).
Sık yapılan hata: if'ten sonra will kullanmak. “If it will rain” değil, If it rains denir.
explain.en:
If sentences describe a condition and its result.
Real possibility: if + present, will + verb (If it rains, I will stay home). Imaginary situation: if + past, would + verb (If I had money, I would travel).
Common mistake: using will after if. Say If it rains, not “If it will rain”.

tip.tr: Edilgen yapı be + üçüncü fiil (V3) ile kurulur. Şimdiki zamanda is/are, geçmişte was/were kullanılır. Örnek: The cake was eaten (Pasta yenildi).

explain.tr:
Edilgen yapı, işi yapandan çok işin kendisi önemliyse kullanılır.
Kalıp: be + üçüncü fiil (V3). Şimdiki zamanda is/are, geçmişte was/were (The cake was eaten).
İşi yapanı söylemek istersek by ekleriz: The book was written by her.
Sık yapılan hata: be fiilini unutmak. “The door locked” değil, The door is locked denir.
explain.en:
The passive is used when the action matters more than who did it.
Pattern: be + past participle (V3). Use is/are in the present and was/were in the past (The cake was eaten).
To name the doer, add by: The book was written by her.
Common mistake: forgetting “be”. Say The door is locked, not “The door locked”.

tip.tr: who kişiler, which/that şeyler, where yerler, whose ise aitlik için kullanılır. Örnek: The man who lives here is a doctor.

explain.tr:
Bir ismi daha ayrıntılı anlatmak için kullanılır.
Who kişiler için, which/that şeyler için, where yerler için, whose aitlik için kullanılır: The man who lives here is a doctor.
İngilizcede ilgi cümlesi isimden sonra gelir, Türkçedeki gibi önce gelmez.
Sık yapılan hata: who'dan sonra kişiyi tekrar etmek. “The man who he lives here” değil, The man who lives here.
explain.en:
Relative clauses give more detail about a noun.
Use who for people, which/that for things, where for places and whose for belonging: The man who lives here is a doctor.
In English the clause comes after the noun, not before it as in Turkish.
Common mistake: repeating the person after who. Say The man who lives here, not “The man who he lives here”.

explain.tr:
Dolaylı anlatım, birinin söylediğini sonradan aktarmak için kullanılır.
Aktaran fiil geçmişteyse zaman genellikle bir adım geriye gider: am/is → was, will → would, do → did.
Örnek: “I am tired” → She said that she was tired.
Sık yapılan hata: Zamanı geri götürmeyi unutmak. “She said she is tired” yerine She said she was tired denir.
explain.en:
Reported speech tells what someone said earlier.
When the reporting verb is in the past, the tense usually moves one step back: am/is → was, will → would, do → did.
Example: “I am tired” → She said that she was tired.
Common mistake: forgetting to shift the tense. Say She said she was tired, not “She said she is tired”.

tip.tr: Şimdiki pişmanlık için I wish + geçmiş zaman, geçmişteki pişmanlık için I wish + had + V3 veya should have + V3 kullanılır. Örnek: I should have studied.

items.text: I wish we had left earlier.

explain.tr:
Wish, istediğin ama olmayan durumlar ve pişmanlıklar için kullanılır.
Şimdiki durum: I wish + geçmiş zaman (I wish I had more time). Geçmiş pişmanlık: I wish + had + V3 ya da should have + V3 (I should have studied).
Sık yapılan hata: Şimdi için geçmiş zaman kullanmayı yanlış sanmak. “I wish I have a car” değil, I wish I had a car denir.
explain.en:
Wish is used for things you want but do not have, and for regrets.
Present situation: I wish + past tense (I wish I had more time). Past regret: I wish + had + V3, or should have + V3 (I should have studied).
Common mistake: using the present tense after wish. Say I wish I had a car, not “I wish I have a car”.
